title: Distinct — Removing Duplicates
description: Learn to remove duplicate elements from collections using the Distinct operator.

data.text: The `Distinct` extension method returns a new collection of unique elements from the given collection, removing any duplicates.

data.title: Distinct with Primitive Types
data.content: Removing duplicates from primitive type collections

data.text: The `Distinct` method doesn't compare values of complex type objects by default. You need to implement `IEqualityComparer<T>` to compare values of complex types:

data.title: Distinct with Custom Comparer
data.content: Removing duplicates from complex type collections

data.title: Not Supported in Query Syntax
data.text: The Distinct operator is not supported in C# query syntax. Use method syntax or call Distinct() on a query variable.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Distinct removes duplicate elements from a collection
Not supported in C# query syntax
data.takeaway: Continue to the next lesson to learn about the Except operator.
